request.prompt: Which humanoid robots can be purchased in North America?

result.text:
As of October 2026, several manufacturers offer humanoid robots for purchase in North America, primarily in the United States. They range from relatively affordable research robots costing around $5,000 to industrial platforms costing well over $100,000.

The most important distinction is between robots that you can actually order and robots that are only available through enterprise partnerships or pilot programs.

1. Humanoid robots available for purchase

These are the most interesting options currently on the market.

1. Unitree R1

Available to order

$8,990+

Indicative US dealer pricing

Compact humanoid, approximately 1.2 m tall.

Walking, movement and AI development.

Basic and EDU configurations.

Primarily a research and development platform.

Website: Unitree Robotics

2. Unitree G1

Available to order

$17,990+

Indicative US dealer pricing

Approximately 1.3 m tall.

23–43 degrees of freedom, depending on configuration.

Advanced walking, manipulation and balance.

EDU versions offer more extensive development capabilities.

Probably one of the strongest options for independent robotics development.

Website: Unitree Robotics

3. Unitree H2

Dealer availability

$39,900+

Indicative US dealer pricing

Full-size humanoid, approximately 1.8 m tall.

More human-like proportions.

Designed for advanced robotics and AI research.

More substantial physical platform than the R1 or G1.

Website: Unitree Robotics

4. 1X NEO

Preorder

$20,000

Or $499/month, according to advertised ordering terms

Designed specifically for household environments.

Approximately 1.65 m tall.

Intended for household chores and assistance.

More consumer-oriented than the Unitree platforms.

Human assistance/teleoperation is part of its development approach.

Website: 1X Technologies

5. Booster K1

Dealer inquiry

~$6,000+

Advertised starting price; availability varies

Compact bipedal robot.

Designed for research, education and robotics development.

Smaller and less expensive than full-size humanoids.

Website: Booster Robotics

4. Important North American purchasing consideration

There is an additional complication for US buyers in 2026.

The FCC introduced restrictions on new equipment authorizations for certain foreign-produced advanced robotics on July 28, 2026. Existing models with qualifying pre-cutoff authorizations can still be sold and imported. This is why the Unitree R1, G1 and H2 are particularly interesting: they have qualifying pre-cutoff FCC records.

Before purchasing any other imported humanoid, request written confirmation of its FCC authorization and import eligibility. Canadian requirements should also be checked separately.
